_comment: Nevada 2026 QAP, Nevada Housing Division, adopted 12/24/2025 and amended 3/25/2026 (cover, p.1). Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed page numbers. Two scoring systems, recorded as two tracks. The DEFAULT track is Section 7, Project Scoring for 9% LIHTCs, pp.24-36. The BOND track is Section 8.2, Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications, pp.37-38, which decides access to Division resources (GAHP funds, Nevada transferable state tax credits) rather than 4% credits themselves. The 9% track DOES NOT RECONCILE, and the mismatch is recorded, not closed. Section 7.1.1 states 'The maximum number of points is 97.' The itemised maxima of 7.3 and 7.4 alone sum to 99 (7.3: 5+5+8+2+4+5+3+16+21 = 69; 7.4: 6+2+6+5+3+8 = 30), before any of 7.2's Project Type Priority points, which pay 10 to the top-ranked project in each category (15 in Tribal Housing) plus 1 for a veterans preference. The computed total of 115 counts 7.2 at its 15-point Tribal maximum, the veterans point, and 7.3.9 at its stated cap of 21. No combination of the document's own section maxima produces 97, and nothing in the document explains the difference; the reviewer should confirm against pp.24-36. Four further internal defects are recorded in notes rather than fixed: 7.1.1 sends deductions to 'Section 21', which does not exist (deductions are in Section 16, p.42); 7.2.6 sends ties to 'Section 7.15', which does not exist (tie breakers are 7.5); 7.4.6 says applications can meet 'three factors below' and then lists two; and 7.3.9.B's acquisition/rehab ladder has no row for $120,001-$134,999 in Clark County. Tribal Housing projects get no amenity points (7.3.3), so their real ceiling differs from everyone else's. Thresholds are in NV_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: Section 7.1.1, p.24: 'The maximum number of points is 97.' MISMATCH, recorded not resolved. The stated section maxima of 7.3 (69) and 7.4 (30) sum to 99 before 7.2's project type priority points. The computed 115 is 99 + 15 (7.2 at its largest value, Tribal Housing) + 1 (7.2.7 veterans preference). A non-Tribal project's ceiling is 110 (99 + 10 + 1); a Tribal project's is 107, because Tribal projects are barred from the 8 amenity points (99 - 8 + 15 + 1). Neither equals 97, and 97 is not reachable by dropping any whole section: excluding all of 7.2 still leaves 99. The gap matters beyond bookkeeping, because p.6 requires applications to 'earn at least 60% of the available points', and 60% of 97 is 58.2 while 60% of 110 is 66. A reviewer should confirm the 97 against p.24 and each section maximum against pp.26-36.

Section 8.2, pp.37-38: 'Total Available 40'. These are additional points on top of a base of 60 that every project receives once it meets the Section 6 pre-application thresholds: 'All projects will start with 60 points ... Additional points will be capped at 40, for a maximum total score of 100 points.' The base is not coded as a criterion because nothing is scored to earn it. The five criteria sum to exactly 40. Four deductions follow the table and sit outside the 40.

groups.label: Project type priorities, one per project category
groups.source_quote: Each applicant must select one project category for which its application will be considered.
groups.note: Section 4 (p.12) requires one project category per application, and 7.2 pays preference points within that category only, so the eight category priorities are alternatives. max_one records 15, the Tribal Housing value; every other category pays 10. Section 1.1 (p.7) says applicants 'must check all category and geographic boxes for which they elect to compete', which reads as permitting more than one category; recorded here as a tension for the reviewer, coded on the Section 4 sentence because it is specific to project categories. 7.2.7 Veterans Preference is not a Section 4 category and sits outside this group.

groups.label: Superior Project, capped at 21
groups.note: The eight lettered items A-H total 30 (4 + 8 + 2 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 2 + 5) against a stated maximum of 21 on p.34.

criteria.heading: Senior housing age 55 and older
criteria.quote: Senior Housing Age 55 and Older.

tiers.tier_label: Lowest average unit size, not below 550 sq. ft. (1-bedroom) / 750 sq. ft. (2-bedroom)

criteria.note: Ranked within each geographic sub-account: only the two best applications in the category score, and every other senior application scores 0 here. The text is internally awkward: it rewards the 'lowest average unit size of no less than 550 sq. ft.' and then says projects 'of no less than 550 sq. feet or closest to 590 sq. ft/unit will receive 10 points', so it is unclear whether the target is the smallest unit size or the one closest to 590. A reviewer should read p.25. New construction studios and one-bedrooms are capped at 650 sq. ft., two-bedrooms at 850, and two-bedrooms at 20% of units.

criteria.heading: Special needs housing projects
criteria.quote: The highest score as calculated above will receive 10 points; the second highest score will receive 5 points.

tiers.tier_label: Highest experience score (0.70 x months of experience + 0.30 x housing units developed)

criteria.note: Scores the sponsor rather than the project: months of experience serving the population weighted 70% and housing units produced weighted 30%, with a worked example on p.25 (175.8 against 148.8). Entry to this category is gated on scoring at least 4 points in 7.4.3 Resident Services.

criteria.heading: Projects for individuals
criteria.quote: New construction projects for individuals must be Studio, 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom units.

tiers.tier_label: Lowest average unit size, not below 550 sq. ft.

criteria.note: Ranked within the category; only the top two score. Average square footage may not exceed 670 sq. ft., studios are capped at 50% of units and two-bedrooms at 10%.

criteria.heading: Projects for individuals with children / families
criteria.quote: New construction projects will be ranked on the most efficient use of space.

tiers.tier_label: Average unit size at or closest to 950 sq. ft.

criteria.note: Ranked within the category; only the top two score. The first-place test is closeness to 950 sq. ft., but second place goes to 'the next lowest unit size', so the two places are not measured the same way.

criteria.heading: Mixed income projects
criteria.quote: The project with the highest percentage of market rate units will receive 10

tiers.tier_label: Highest percentage of market-rate units above the 10% minimum

criteria.note: Ranked within the category; only the top two score. Market-rate and restricted units must be proportional in size and bedroom count.

criteria.heading: Mixed use (or multi use) projects
criteria.quote: The Division will rank Mixed Use Project applications based on the highest residential square footage.
criteria.note: Ranked within the category; only the top two score. Ties go to 'the Tie Breakers Section (Section 7.15)', which does not exist; the tie breakers are Section 7.5 on p.36. Recorded as a cross-reference error in the document.

criteria.heading: Housing for veterans; veterans preference
criteria.quote: NHD will award 1 point for providing a preference of a minimum of 10% of the total number of restricted
criteria.note: Not ranked against the round, and not a Section 4 project category, so it sits outside the project type group and can be earned alongside a category priority. A tenant selection preference for veteran households covering at least 10% of units, without designating particular units. USDA-RD projects are not eligible.

criteria.heading: New construction projects utilizing alternative materials/methods
criteria.quote: The project with the lowest development cost per unit will receive 10 preference points

tiers.tier_label: Lowest total development cost per unit, at or under $330,000

criteria.note: Storage container conversions, modular and manufactured housing. Only projects at or under $330,000 per unit are eligible. CONTRADICTION, recorded not resolved: 7.2 on p.24 says 'Eventual tenant ownership projects are not eligible for scoring in Section 7.2' and, in the next sentence, that 'Rent to own projects will only receive points under the category described in Section 7.2.8'. Section 4.8 defines Rent to Own as Housing for Eventual Tenant Ownership, so the two sentences exclude and admit the same projects. 7.2.8 itself ('This includes Rent to Own projects') and 4.12 ('Rent to own projects will only be eligible for the 10/5 preference points in this category') both side with admitting them. A reviewer should confirm.

criteria.heading: Housing for tribal governments
criteria.quote: will receive 15 points, the project with the second lowest amount will receive 5 points.
criteria.note: The only project type priority worth 15 rather than 10. Scored on credits per bedroom, with the worked example $1,100,000 / 80 bedrooms = $13,750. Offset by 7.3.3, which gives Tribal Housing projects no amenity points 'to address the inflated costs in Tribal Housing projects'.

criteria.heading: Project location
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM LOCATION POINTS

tiers.tier_label: In a Qualified Census Tract and covered by a state or local Concerted Community Revitalization Plan
In a non-CDBG eligible census tract

criteria.note: Two unrelated routes to the same 5 points, capped at 5: one rewards a QCT covered by a revitalization plan, the other a tract that is not CDBG-eligible. A CCRP must pre-date the application, have components beyond this project, and be evidenced by a local government resolution.

criteria.heading: Site control
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM PROJECT READINESS POINTS

tiers.tier_label: General partner or managing member holds fee simple title to land and improvements
Long-term lease, Tribal Housing and Public Housing Authority only: 15-20 years for rent to own, otherwise not less than 50 years

criteria.note: Headed Site Control but totalled as 'MAXIMUM PROJECT READINESS POINTS'. A purchase contract or option, which satisfies the 6.8 threshold, earns nothing here: the points require title or, for tribes and PHAs, a long lease.

criteria.heading: Additional and threshold project amenities
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM AMENITIES POINTS

tiers.tier_label: Project: grills, picnic tables and slabs scaled to unit count
Project: swimming or lap pool, projects over 50 units
Project: 500 sq. ft. community room, family projects of 39 units or less
Project: library or reading room with 50 books
Project: automatic openers on common area doors
Unit: air conditioning (outside Clark County only)
Unit: attached two-car garage (tenant ownership) or covered parking
Unit: washer/dryer hookups, family projects of 39 units or less
Unit: ceiling fans in living room and master bedroom
Unit: covered front porch (tenant ownership only)
Unit: entry screen front door (tenant ownership only)
Unit: two garage storage cabinets (tenant ownership only)
Unit: garage storage shelves (tenant ownership only)
Unit: garage door opener (tenant ownership only)
Unit: removable cabinet fronts (special needs and senior only)
Unit: 21% of units adaptable/accessible, exceeding the 5% and 2% requirement
Unit: grab bars in all units specified for handicapped use

criteria.note: A menu, not a checklist: ten project amenities worth 24 and twenty-two unit amenities worth 41, 65 in all, against a cap of 8. Every value was read from the text layer and checked against the rendered pages 27-29. Recreation areas are 'worth 1.5 points each' in the text and 3 in the points column, so two recreation areas reach the row maximum. Amenities shared with another phase or an adjacent project earn half value, and amenities that are required by the threshold table on p.29 earn nothing. Tribal Housing projects are barred from amenity points entirely. Acquisition/rehabilitation projects may also earn points for upgrading existing amenities identified in the Capital Needs Assessment, at values the section does not state.

criteria.heading: Nevada based applicant
criteria.quote: Up to two (2) points will be awarded to projects if the Applicant or Co-Applicant is based in Nevada.
criteria.note: 'Up to two' in the prose but the table has a single 2-point row, so this is all or nothing. A business entity must be organized under Nevada law and have existed for 12 months (a gate shaded as a threshold row), maintain a Nevada office from which a principal officer conducts business, and keep staff there available to the public.

criteria.heading: Affordability period
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM AFFORDABILITY PERIOD POINTS
criteria.note: One point per additional 5-year period of affordability, capped at 4, so the maximum is reached at 20 extra years. The prose says 'not to exceed 50 years', which is the Section 6.2 ceiling on the extended use period rather than a scoring limit. Tenant ownership projects are excluded from extending under 6.2.

criteria.heading: Water efficiency of landscape design
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM LANDSCAPING DESIGN POINTS
criteria.note: All or nothing: architect or landscape architect verification of at least 75% desert and/or xeriscape landscaping. The rating row's own points cell is shaded and empty; the 5 is the stated maximum.

criteria.heading: Historical character
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM HISTORIC CHARACTER POINTS
criteria.note: Adapting or renovating a property on the National or State Register, as determined by the State Historic Preservation Office in a letter. The table header has no POINTS column label and the rating row's cell is shaded; the 3 is the stated maximum on p.31.

criteria.heading: Smart designs
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM SMART DESIGN POINTS

tiers.tier_label: Within 1/2 mile of at least three listed services
Within 1/2 mile of a designated pedestrian/bicycle path
Transit: Clark and Washoe, 0.25 mile to a weekday 7am-7pm bus stop or a school bus stop; other counties, 1/2 mile to a transit route or school bus stop
Energy Star or equivalent certification, or a rehab scope exceeding the minimum improvement requirement

criteria.note: The five items sum to exactly the stated 16. Item A is headed 'Site Location - Up to five points will be awarded', but the three site location items beneath it total 4, so the 5 is never binding unless items 4 and 5 are meant to sit under A as well, which the layout does not make clear. A reviewer should check p.31. USDA funding is worth as much as all three location items and more than half the section; it is a funding-source test filed under Smart Designs.

criteria.heading: Lowest LIHTC requested per person
criteria.quote: The project with the lowest amount of LIHTCs requested per person receives 4

tiers.tier_label: Lowest credits per person in the region

criteria.note: Available to two projects in each of Clark County, Washoe County and Other Counties. Persons are 1.5 per bedroom and 1.0 per studio. Taking these points probably has a later cost: p.9 limits projects that 'received points for most efficient use of LIHTCs under Superior Project' to additional credits of 6% of the original allocation, against 12% for everyone else. 'Most efficient use of LIHTCs' is read here as this item; the p.9 sentence does not name the letter.

criteria.heading: Total development cost per unit, excluding land
criteria.quote: Total development cost per unit, excluding land costs:

tiers.tier_label: Clark, acquisition/rehab line item: $135,000 or more
Other counties, Tribal new construction: under $510,000
Other counties, other new construction: under $340,000
Other counties, acquisition/rehab line item (USDA included): under $100,000
Other counties, acquisition/rehab line item: $130,000 or more

criteria.note: Six separate ladders by region and project type, so a project is scored against one. Values read from the text layer and checked against the rendered p.33, where the points column says only 'From 0 Up to a maximum of 8'. The Clark County acquisition/rehab ladder skips $120,001-$134,999, so a project in that band has no row, and then awards 1 point at '$135,000 or more', above the $120,000 maximum rehab line item that Section 6.4 (p.17) sets for Clark County. The other-counties rehab ladder awards its 1 point at '$130,000 or more', which is the 6.4 maximum for those counties. Recorded, not resolved; the reviewer should check whether the top rehab rows are meant to be reachable without a 6.4 waiver. Each new construction ladder's 1-point row ends exactly at the 6.4 cost limit.

criteria.heading: Foreclosed, vacant or abandoned building, or non-residential conversion
criteria.quote: Project includes the acquisition/rehabilitation of a foreclosed, vacant, or
criteria.note: Adaptive reuse and distressed-property acquisition share one 2-point row.

criteria.heading: Preservation of existing LIHTC units
criteria.quote: Project includes the preservation of existing LIHTC units
criteria.note: Excludes USDA-RD projects, which have their own 5-point route at 7.3.9.E.

criteria.heading: Preservation project with USDA-RD letter of support
criteria.quote: Any preservation project with a letter of support from the USDA-RD office.
criteria.note: Worth more than the general LIHTC preservation row (2). Taken together with the 6 points for USDA funding in 7.3.8, a USDA preservation deal collects 11 points that are unavailable to any other project.

criteria.heading: Project-based rental assistance on at least 25% of units
criteria.quote: At least 25% of the units receiving Project Based Rental Assistance
criteria.note: Verified by a Housing Assistance Payment contract.

criteria.heading: Owner-paid utilities
criteria.quote: Project Sponsor will pay electric, gas, and heating and/or cooling utility
criteria.note: The sponsor pays electric, gas, and heating and/or cooling charges.

criteria.heading: New construction of minimum size
criteria.quote: New Construction developments in Clark County with a minimum of 50 units
criteria.note: At least 50 units in Clark County, 30 elsewhere. A scale test inside a section otherwise about cost and preservation.

criteria.heading: Low rent targeting
criteria.quote: Points will be awarded by multiplying the percentage of the total restricted units within each level(s) by the

tiers.tier_label: All projects except rent to own: weighted average rent level under 40%
Rent to own only: 60%-100% of units at 60% income rent level or below
Rent to own only: less than 100% of units at 60% income rent level or below

criteria.note: Two ladders, one for rent to own projects and one for everything else, each with a maximum of 6. The weighted average is the share of restricted units at each rent level times that level, with a worked example on p.34 (0.4313 for 15 units at 40% and 25 at 45%). A weighted average at 50% or above earns nothing. The rent to own rows are hard to parse: '60% - 100% of units' at the top tier, and '>60% - Projects with less than 100% of units' at the second; a reviewer should read p.34.

criteria.heading: Low-income targeting
criteria.quote: Two (2) points for a signed letter agreeing to restrict rents/and incomes to not exceed the 50% limit for all
criteria.note: All LIHTC units at or below 50% of AMI. Overlaps 7.4.1, which a 50% ceiling alone does not reach: 7.4.1 pays only below a 50% weighted average.

criteria.heading: Resident services
criteria.quote: A maximum of six (6) points based on the number of resident services provided to tenants.

tiers.tier_label: On-site van service, at least two days a week
On-site service coordinator, at least 10 hours a week
On-site service coordinator, at least 20 hours a week
MOU with a service provider with 3 years' experience, at least 15 hours a week on site

criteria.note: Items total 12 against a cap of 6. The two service coordinator rows read as alternative levels of one service; the van and MOU rows are additive. The MOU row carries no letter in the table. Services must run for the full 15-year compliance period with no gap over 30 days. Scoring at least 4 here is the gate for competing in the 7.2.2 Special Needs category.

criteria.heading: Lowest developer fees
criteria.quote: One point for each 1% reduction in developer fee
criteria.note: Measured against the 15% developer fee ceiling in Section 6.6. The table leaves exactly 15.00% unassigned, which is harmless in practice because it scores 0 either way. No 'MAXIMUM' row; the 5 is from the prose 'up to a maximum of five'.

criteria.heading: Low contractor fee
criteria.quote: One point for each 1% reduction in Contractor Fees, up to a maximum of three, based on figures provided
criteria.note: Measured against the 14% contractor fee limit in Section 6.6. Contractor fee includes profit, overhead and general requirements, and may rise later only if the percentage claimed is held to three decimal places.

criteria.heading: Arm's length transfer of real estate at nominal cost
criteria.quote: An arm’s length transfer of real estate to the Applicant/Co-Applicants for a nominal

tiers.tier_label: Price over 1% and up to 5% of fair market value

criteria.note: The bottom band is printed '> $1% and ≤ 5% of FMV', with a stray dollar sign; read as 1%. A transfer at 1% of value or less falls outside every band as written. 7.4.6 introduces 'three factors below' and lists only A and B; recorded as a defect in the document. A and B together make the stated 8.

criteria.heading: Leveraged public and third-party funding sources
criteria.quote: MAXIMUM AFFORDABLE HOUSING INCENTIVE POINTS
criteria.note: Eligible sources are the local PHA, CDBG, HUD 202/811 or USDA-RD 515, FHLB AHP, local housing funds (HOME, LIHTF, NHTF, RDA), tribal and BIA sources for Indian housing, and third-party non-mortgage grants; others need advance written approval each year. The bottom tier pays 1 point for any qualifying source at all, and the text leaves 20.001%-20.01% unassigned.

criteria.heading: Lowest ten-year credits as a share of total project cost
criteria.quote: The project with the lowest percentage to two decimal places will win the
criteria.note: Gross ten-year credits divided by total project costs; the worked example is $8,000,000 / $10,000,000 = 80.00%. A lottery under NAC 319.990 follows if that fails, and an application that received a waiver loses any tie.

criteria.heading: Compliance history deduction
criteria.quote: An application may lose five points instead of being ineligible based on outstanding compliance violations.
criteria.note: A deduction offered in lieu of ineligibility, for non-compliance unresolved beyond the 90-day cure period. 7.1.1 says deductions are 'set forth in Section 21'; there is no Section 21, and the general deductions are in Section 16.

criteria.heading: Score reduction for application or applicant defects
criteria.quote: the Division may reject an application or reduce the score
criteria.note: 'Up to 10 points', at the Division's choice as an alternative to rejection, for eleven listed circumstances ranging from an incomplete application to felony conviction, foreclosure, unpaid fees and failure to place in service. The list is numbered 3) to 13), with no 1) or 2).

criteria.heading: Deduction for requesting a QAP waiver
criteria.quote: Projects requesting waivers of any requirement of this QAP will have a 3-point deduction in their application
criteria.note: Applies to any waiver, including the cost limit waivers that 6.4 invites for large-family and high-need rehabilitation projects. A waiver also loses any tie under 7.5.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Weighted average AMI below 60%
criteria.quote: excluding any market rate units
criteria.note: Calculated the same way as the 9% weighted average in 7.4.1, excluding market-rate units. The bond ladder starts where the 9% ladder stops: 9% pays nothing at 50% and above, bond pays its full 10 just below 50%.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Site location
criteria.quote: Proximity to Services and Important Facilities: 1 point

tiers.tier_label: Within 0.5 miles of at least three listed services
Public transportation: 0.25 miles to a bus stop in Clark and Washoe, 0.5 mile elsewhere; school bus stops for family projects
Infill: previously developed, or at least 50% of the perimeter adjoining developed urban uses

criteria.note: The three items sum to the stated 3. Infill is scored here but nowhere in the 9% track.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: BLM land or other public land donation
criteria.quote: BLM Land or other public land
criteria.note: No test is stated beyond the row label.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Leverage of other public or private resources
criteria.quote: Leverage of other public or

tiers.tier_label: Other public or philanthropic financing: AHP, HOME, local fee waivers or incentives

criteria.note: Over half the bond track. The pricing ladder is alternative and the other-financing award ('Up to 7 points') is additive on top, reaching 23. The pricing ladder is headed 'exceeds $0.84 cents per credit' and then pays 4 points above $0.82, so the heading and the ladder disagree about where points start; the ladder is coded. Pricing below $0.80 is separately a 20-point deduction, which leaves $0.80-$0.82 earning nothing and losing nothing. The test for the 'up to 7' is not stated.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Nonprofit / housing authority owner
criteria.quote: Nonprofit / Housing Authority
criteria.note: No test beyond the row label.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Compliance / QC history deduction
criteria.quote: Compliance / QC History (loss of up to 25 points)
criteria.note: Up to 25 points. QC is Qualified Contract; every applicant also signs a waiver of the Qualified Contract process under 6.2.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Federal credit pricing below $0.80 deduction
criteria.quote: Federal Tax Credit Pricing below $0.80 (loss of 20 points)
criteria.note: A fixed 20 points, not 'up to'. In the text layer this bullet runs straight into the next one without a break.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Uncertain plan of finance deduction
criteria.quote: finance and/or funding sources (loss of up to 10 points)
criteria.note: Up to 10 points, including for projects that have not chosen equity and senior lending partners or that rely on public funds not yet awarded.

criteria.native_category: Scoring for Tax Exempt Bond Project Applications
criteria.heading: Cost per unit deduction
criteria.quote: acquisition rehab (loss of up to 5 points)
criteria.note: Up to 5 points where cost per unit exceeds $435,000 for new construction or $375,000 for acquisition rehab. Rebuilds and extensive rehab may be treated as new construction.
